mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption pullback offset by a housing rebound, resulting in flat to mildly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate remains below 4% indicates a supply-side shock in a tight labor market, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply disruption
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% signals an exceptionally tight labor market, which historically precedes a moderation in earnings growth and lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which typically depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
